title: Why functions exist
learningObjectives: Explain why functions exist and write reusable JavaScript functions or control flow.

understand.concept: Functions package reusable instructions into named or callable units. They can accept inputs, perform work, and return outputs. Functions help separate responsibilities, reduce duplication, and make programs easier to test.
understand.whyItMatters: Without functions, repeated logic becomes scattered and changes must be made in multiple places. Small focused functions support reuse and clearer reasoning.
understand.analogy: A function is a named recipe: provide ingredients, follow the steps, and receive a result.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; JavaScript execution, hoisting, and parameter evaluation follow language rules.

explain.narrative: The function accepts price and quantity and returns their product, which is 75.

examples.explanation: The function accepts price and quantity and returns their product, which is 75.
examples.expectedOutput: The browser console displays the function or control-flow result described.

practise.guidedTask: Write a function that converts minutes to seconds. Call it with several values and explain its inputs and output.
practise.independentTask: Create a small program that uses the control structure or function concept. Test normal, boundary, and optional-input cases.
hints: Keep inputs explicit and return results where practical.

practice.starterCode:
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en"><head><meta charset="utf-8"><meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1"><title>Why functions exist</title></head><body>
<script>function calculateTotal(price,quantity){return price*quantity;}console.log(calculateTotal(25,3));</script>
</body></html>

questions.prompt: What is one main benefit of using functions?
questions.explanation: Functions help organise, reuse, and test program behaviour.

questions.prompt: What makes a function easier to reuse and test?
options: Clear inputs, focused responsibility, and explicit results
Hidden global state and unrelated side effects
A very long function with many unrelated tasks
questions.answer: Clear inputs, focused responsibility, and explicit results
questions.explanation: Focused functions with clear inputs and outputs are easier to reason about and test.
